bullets.title: Intel massive earnings beat: EPS $0.42 vs $0.21 est, revenue $16.1B vs $14.4B est
bullets.body: Intel reported Q2 EPS of $0.42 vs $0.21 consensus (100% beat) and revenue of $16.1B vs $14.43B expected, with Q3 guidance of $15.8-16.8B vs $15.06B est and adj EPS $0.38 vs $0.27. CFO signals 2026 capex rising to $20B from $18B with 2027 capex 'up meaningfully'; Intel locked 10+ long-term customer agreements and is undershipping data center customers by significant margin. Stock initially surged 10-11% AH before paring gains to ~3%.

bullets.title: Intel foundry inflection: 18A-P enters risk production; 14A high-volume ramp committed for 2028
bullets.body: Intel's 18A-P process is entering risk production for external customers, and management formally committed to a high-volume ramp in 2028 during the Q2 call. Early work on Intel 14A continues to make good progress with IP portfolio buildout confirmed. CFO also notes foundry is two businesses—wafers and advanced packaging—with early customer traction on the packaging side. Intel reportedly entering memory business (ZAM/XBM) per CEO comment.

bullets.title: TSLA plunges 14.5%, worst day since March 2025, on autonomy scale-up caution
bullets.body: Tesla fell 14.5% after management cautioned against scaling unsupervised autonomy until ~40 test vehicles demonstrate safety, while providing no key metrics (paid unsupervised rides, AV unit count). Waymo operates 3,500 unsupervised AVs vs Tesla's ~40, generating 500K paid rides/week vs Tesla's 4K. Short sellers banked $4.1-4.3B on the move, and TSLA options showed the most bearish flow of any name on the day.

bullets.title: GOOGL breaks 200-day MA for first time in over a year on $185B capex shock
bullets.body: Alphabet fell 7.1% and broke its 200-day moving average for the first time in over a year, erasing ~$300B in market cap. The stock is down 13% on the week. Alphabet plans $185B capex in 2026, more than doubling prior year, while Google token growth decelerated to 38% QoQ from 60% prior quarter—a 22pp deceleration raising monetization questions. Google's Anthropic stake is now valued at $124B.

bullets.title: Mag-7 suffers worst single-day collective selloff in 5 years; S&P below 50-day MA by widest margin since April
bullets.body: The Mag-7 basket fell 4.80% in one of its largest down days in years, with every member down more than 1.5%. S&P 500 (SPY) closed below its 50-day moving average by the largest margin since April; S&P 500 on track for first red July since 2014. GOOGL broke trade and trend; TSLA bearish; MSFT failed another trend transition; AAPL is the lone Mag-7 bright spot.

bullets.title: AMD launches Instinct MI455X (320B transistors, 50% more HBM4 than NVIDIA Rubin) and EPYC Venice CPUs outperform NVIDIA Vera 20% single-core
bullets.body: AMD unveiled the Instinct MI455X GPU with 320B transistors and 40 PFLOPs of AI compute, claiming 50% more HBM4 memory than NVIDIA's Rubin alternative. AMD EPYC Venice CPUs are reportedly 20% faster in single-core and deliver 2.2x higher throughput vs NVIDIA Vera, with 256 Zen 6 cores and 203B transistors at 5GHz+. AMD CEO Lisa Su raised the server CPU TAM to $200B by 2030, tripling the $60B estimate from November 2025.

bullets.title: AMD-Cerebras partnership: disaggregated inference targets 5x better token/watt vs NVIDIA Groq
bullets.body: AMD and Cerebras introduced a disaggregated inference solution pairing the Cerebras Wafer-Scale Engine with AMD's Helios platform, claiming 5x higher tokens-per-second-per-watt vs NVIDIA's Groq positioning. AMD's Venice and MI455X are in production at TSMC on 2nm using CoWoS-L packaging (capacity still tight). Channel checks suggest AMD may pursue CPO for future Helios generations, and Anthropic confirmed it will use AMD CPUs and GPUs across clouds and neoclouds.

bullets.title: TSMC 3nm fully booked through 2027; Tesla AI6.5 chip first 2nm in Arizona; Tesla AI5 for Optimus in mass production mid-2027
bullets.body: TSMC's 3nm process has full visibility through 2027 with orders from Qualcomm (Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5) and Tesla (AI5 for Optimus/automotive mass production by mid-2027). Tesla's AI6.5 chip will be TSMC's first 2nm production in Arizona, with Global Unichip as design partner for AI5. CoWoS-L packaging capacity remains constrained.

bullets.title: NVIDIA prepays $1.5B to Amkor for US chip packaging; GPU residual value guarantees enable bank financing of AI clusters
bullets.body: NVIDIA signed a $1.5B strategic partnership with Amkor Technology focused on advanced semiconductor packaging and test technologies for next-generation AI chips in the US. Separately, NVIDIA is implementing residual value guarantees (price floors) on GPUs, converting previously unbankable speculative AI clusters into financeable projects. Nvidia's 800V HVDC architecture enters production in 1Q27 with Delta ramp in 2Q.

bullets.title: SK Hynix develops 3D-stacked DRAM for on-device AI; Apple speculated as North American partner
bullets.body: SK Hynix is accelerating development of 3D-stacked DRAM for on-device AI and recruiting engineers for joint development. One analyst speculates the unnamed North American customer collaborating with SK Hynix is Apple, noting stacked DRAM as prerequisite for widespread on-device AI adoption. Morgan Stanley analyst Shawn Kim's bearish memory call is circulating (unverified) and may have cost the firm the SK Hynix US listing mandate.

bullets.title: GOOGL token growth decelerates sharply; AI monetization questioned as only 2.2% of households pay for AI
bullets.body: Google token growth decelerated to 38% QoQ from 60% in the prior quarter per Hedgeye Tech, a 22pp deceleration raising ROI questions on massive AI capex. Separately, only 2.2% of US households report paying for AI despite hundreds of billions in sector spending, highlighting a monetization gap. US stocks declined on tech earnings raising questions over sustainability of heavy AI investment.

bullets.title: Oil surges 7% to $100+ Brent; rate-hike odds climb; 10-year Treasury breaks 4.7%
bullets.body: Brent crude settled at $100.69/bbl (+7.04%) and WTI at $92.19 (+6.17%) after Houthi attacks on Saudi oil tankers and Trump threatening massive strikes on Iran. Oil volatility (OVX) is breaking higher while equity VIX remains calm. The 10-year Treasury yield broke above 4.7% for the first time since January 2025; 30-year hit 5.18% (19-year high); mortgage rates at 11-month highs. Markets now pricing ~34-36% chance of a Fed rate hike by September and nearly 2 full hikes by year-end.

bullets.title: Japan JGB yields hitting multi-decade highs across the curve; Finance Minister signals FX intervention readiness
bullets.body: Japan's 2-year JGB yield hit a 30-year high at 1.505%; 5-year hit an all-time high of 2.045%; 10-year rose 4bps to 2.810%; 30-year rose 5bps to 3.965%. Japanese Finance Minister Katayama stated authorities are prepared to take decisive action on FX and maintain close 24-hour contact with Washington. Yen is near 40-year lows vs the dollar.

bullets.title: Eurozone PMI surprise: composite at 51.9 vs 50.2 forecast; Germany 51.2 vs 49.8
bullets.body: Eurozone July composite PMI beat consensus at 51.9 vs 50.2 forecast, signaling expansion. Germany's flash composite PMI came in at 51.2 vs 49.8 expected, despite GFK consumer confidence missing at -29.6. UK June retail sales also beat across all measures (inc. auto fuel +4.2% YoY vs 2.4% est; ex-auto/fuel +5.4% YoY vs 3.2% est). ECB inflation expectations fell: 1Y to 3.0% vs 3.2% est.

bullets.title: US initial jobless claims fall to lowest level since 1969; labor market re-tightening
bullets.body: Initial jobless claims dropped to the lowest level since 1969 (Nixon era), reversing the prior cooling trend. One economist notes the labor market is no longer cooling while inflation remains well above the Fed target, adding context to rising rate-hike probabilities.

bullets.title: Trump Section 301 tariffs of 10-12.5% hit 60 countries; oil, gas, food exempted
bullets.body: Trump administration unveiled broad new Section 301 tariffs of 10% (forced-labor-compliant nations) to 12.5% (non-compliant) on 60 trading partners, replacing expiring 10% global duties effective July 24 at 12:01am ET. Oil, gas, fertilizer, foodstuffs, Section 232 goods, and USMCA-compliant products are exempted. EU expressed surprise and will seek answers from Washington; Canada says 'everything on the table' if no deal; Brazil, Australia formally objected.

bullets.title: Oracle wins $3.3B Navy contract plus up to $7B Pentagon software deal
bullets.body: Oracle was awarded a $3.3B 5-year contract with the US Navy for software licensing, maintenance, and SaaS. Separately, Oracle signed a 10-year software contract with the Pentagon worth up to $7B. CEO Larry Ellison has donated $45M to pro-Trump groups and has a $500B 'Stargate' AI data project with the administration.

bullets.title: AAII bullish sentiment collapses 15pp to 29.6%; single-stock vol at 10-year highs relative to index
bullets.body: AAII bullish sentiment plunged 15 percentage points to 29.6% (vs 37.5% historical average), while bearish sentiment surged to 42.3% from 32.9%. Single-stock volatility hit a 10-year high relative to the broad index, with dispersion (not correlation) driving the tape—a market structure inflection point for active managers.

bullets.title: NOK: optical up 20%, IP up 16%, AI orders tripled—earnings stronger than stock reaction suggests
bullets.body: Nokia's Q2 optical segment grew 20% and IP 16% on design-win conversions; AI orders have tripled, making NOK a long-term call option on Jensen's AI-RAN/6G ambitions. One analyst argues the earnings were materially stronger than the stock reaction implies, though macro conditions remain heavy. Skeptics note only a small portion of NOK revenue is currently tied to AI, limiting near-term upside.

bullets.title: Meta secures $12B data center financing at higher borrowing costs; hyperscaler IG spreads widening
bullets.body: Meta faces higher borrowing costs on its latest $12B data center financing round. Separately, one account warns IG bond spreads in the hyperscaler segment are 'exploding every day' with credit investors refusing to fund memory chip purchases, while equity markets have not yet priced the bond market stress.
